concerns.text: T013 (Download) declares a hard failure if <50 datasets are found, yet T052 (Fallback) is listed as a dependency of T013. This creates a logical deadlock: T013 cannot complete to trigger T052 if it fails first. The fallback logic must be internal to T013 or T013 must not fail until T052 has exhausted the secondary list.

T014 (Checksum) is scheduled immediately after T013 (Download) but before T015/T016 (Filtering). T014 checksums 'all downloaded datasets', while T017 (Metadata) only records 'retained' datasets. This violates the data-flow: the final `data/datasets.csv` (retained) will not align with `data/checksums.csv` (all) unless T014 is re-ordered to run AFTER filtering or scoped to only retained files.

T053 (Streaming) is placed in Phase 3 (US1) but depends on T013. However, T024a (US2) and T031a (US4) require computing skew/kurtosis from the 'real-world filtered datasets' (T017) to parameterize simulations. Streaming logic (T053) often prevents full in-memory aggregation required for these statistics. If T053 prevents T017 from calculating global distribution stats, the downstream simulation tasks (T024a, T031a) cannot execute, creating a data-flow break.

T024d and T041c are implementation tasks to 'Update spec.md'. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' principle for the specification artifact. The spec (Producer) must be updated BEFORE the tasks (Consumers) are generated. Including spec-modification as a downstream task implies the spec is not the Single Source of Truth at the time of task generation, breaking the dependency chain for FR-004 and FR-008 alignment.

T004b (Verify Checkpointing) depends on T004. However, T004b is marked [P] (parallel-safe). Verification tasks that read/write state files often have implicit ordering requirements relative to the state they verify. If T004b runs before T004 completes its first write, it will fail. The [P] tag is likely unsafe here; it should be sequential.
